captions.instagram:
What is Coulomb's law?

Two protons push each other apart 10³⁶ times harder than gravity pulls them together. Trace field lines from the charges themselves, twist Coulomb's silver wire from 1785, hang two rubbed balloons, get zapped by a door handle on a dry winter day, stand under a thundercloud, and watch toner leap in a laser printer.

→ Like charges repel: F = k q₁ q₂ ÷ r². Double the distance and the push drops to a quarter.
→ In 1785 Coulomb measured it with a twisting silver wire. Half the distance took four times the twist.
→ With many charges, add the pushes one by one. Field lines trace the total, from plus to minus.
→ Rub two balloons on your hair. Both gain electrons, and like charges push apart.
→ On a dry winter day a walk across a carpet can charge you to 30,000 volts. Then: zap.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/coulombclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: What is Coulomb's law? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Two protons push each other apart 10³⁶ times harder than gravity pulls them together. Trace field lines from the charges themselves, twist Coulomb's silver wire from 1785, hang two rubbed balloons, get zapped by a door handle on a dry winter day, stand under a thundercloud, and watch toner leap in a laser printer.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/coulombclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/coulombclear

In this video:
• Like repels, unlike attracts. F = k q₁ q₂ ÷ r², with k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m²/C².
• Many charges: add the arrows. With several charges, work out each push alone and add them.
• Static at home. Rubbing moves electrons; it never makes charge.
• From thunderclouds to toner. A cloud with ±40 C at 6 and 12 km makes about 15 kV/m at the ground below, and its two charge centres pull on each other with 400 kN.
• Gravity's twin, and the limits. Same shape as gravity, but 1.2 × 10³⁶ times stronger between two protons.
